key_insight: Jointly optimizing request routing and KV-cache retention improves multi-turn LLM serving by balancing compute and memory costs against future prefix-reuse value.
engineering_relevance: PARK translates this optimization into a practical controller for GPU clusters serving agents that alternate between LLM inference and external tool calls.
method: Derive admission, routing, and eviction rules from a fluid model using resource shadow prices and session continuation values.
Use a buffer-reserve policy to absorb stochastic fluctuations with an asymptotically vanishing capacity share.
Implement online price updates, one-turn migration lookahead, and cache retention ranked by expected reuse value per byte-epoch.
evidence_signal: With a 197B-parameter MoE model on 16 H200 GPUs, PARK improved output throughput over the strongest baseline by 24.2% on SWE and 40.0% on Terminal-Bench; 128-GPU experiments sustained 50,789–67,363 output tokens/s.
watch_item: Results cover one model and two agent benchmarks; broader deployment should validate reuse-value estimates and robustness to delayed load reports.
paper_title: Routing and Cache Retention for Multi-Turn LLM Inference: Theory and Implementation
